Will Tom remember the three safety rules? Will the small children be safe?

- stranger — a person you don't know
- danger/dangerous — something or someone that can hurt you
- safe/safety — protected from harm or danger
- evidence — proof that shows something is true (like a photo)
- brave/bravery — doing something even when you are scared
- rules — instructions that keep you safe
- worried — feeling nervous or afraid about something

videos.title: Nana Fell Down and Won't Wake Up | Slow English Listening Practice for Beginners Easy English learn
videos.description:
Nana fell down in the kitchen. She won't wake up. Lily and Tom are home alone — what do they do?
In today's Slow English Story (A1 Level), Lily and Tom are baking chocolate chip cookies with Nana when something goes wrong. Nana feels dizzy, her face goes pale, and suddenly she faints on the kitchen floor. Mom is at the store. Dad is at work. The two children are completely alone. Can they stay calm and get help in time?

This video is perfect for:

English listening practice for beginners
A1 level learners
Learning English through family stories
Slow and clear English speaking practice
English vocabulary building
Shadowing and pronunciation practice


Key Vocabulary in This Episode:

faint — when your body gets too weak and you fall down and cannot stay awake
dizzy — a feeling that everything is moving or spinning around you
pulse — the beat of your heart; you can feel it in your neck
ambulance — a special car with doctors inside that comes to help in an emergency
emergency — a sudden, dangerous situation that needs help very fast
paramedic — a person trained to help sick or hurt people before they reach the hospital
blood pressure — the force of blood moving inside your body; when it is too low, you can faint
steady — calm and regular; not changing fast
